description: pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs:187 — crl_number() returns None for any CRL whose CRLNumber INTEGER is longer than 8 bytes (uint_to_u64 returns None, which is swallowed by .and_then). The with_delta staleness guard (line 187-190) skips the check entirely when crl_number returns None. This means a delta CRL with BaseCRLNumber=9999 would be accepted against a base with an oversized CRLNumber, bypassing the 'delta is newer than base' guard. base_crl_number() uses a different code path (propagates the error via Some(Err(...))), but crl_number() silently discards overflow. In practice PKITS numbers are small, but the asymmetry is a latent correctness bug: the same 'too large to fit in u64' number silently disables the check instead of returning an error.
title: crl_number silently ignores >8-byte CRL numbers in staleness check
